\subsection{InfoGeometry.ExponentialFamily.FiniteExponentialFamilyData}
\noindent\textbf{Topological Vulnerability:} 40 downstream dependencies.\\ 

General finite exponential family as an instance of the ExponentialFamily typeclass.
Given a base measure `P` and sufficient statistic `stat`, the density is:
  P.prob x * exp(θ * stat x) / partition(θ)
where partition(θ) = ∑ x, P.prob x * exp(θ * stat x)
The exponential identity uses `log (P.prob x)` in the statistic.
This data structure includes strict positivity `base_pos`, so this log is always at a positive value.

\subsection{InfoGeometry.Canonical.RGFlow.InformationFlow}
\noindent\textbf{Topological Vulnerability:} 13 downstream dependencies.\\ 

A Renormalization Group (RG) Flow on information manifolds.
This represents the evolution of the belief geometry as the 'resolution' 
of the data changes (coarse-graining).

\subsection{InfoGeometry.Canonical.BeliefDynamics.radonNikodymOp}
\noindent\textbf{Topological Vulnerability:} 3 downstream dependencies.\\ 

The Radon-Nikodym Operator (Information Density Ratio).
L(x, y) = exp(ψ(x) - ψ(y) - <∇ψ(y), x - y>).
This is exactly the exponential of the negative Bregman divergence.
It represents the 'belief likelihood' ratio between two states.

\subsection{InfoGeometry.Canonical.GrandSynthesis.cl11\_bottDirac\_sq\_eq\_metricOp\_form}
\noindent\textbf{Topological Vulnerability:} 1 downstream dependencies.\\ 

Lichnerowicz-style bridge in the current framework:
for `InfoSpectralTriple`, `D²` rewrites to the Hessian metric operator, and therefore
the split Bott-Dirac square rewrites to the corresponding metric-op Laplacian form.

and a key embedding, the total multi-head output decomposes into the sum of:
1. The output-projected query embeddings (the global skip connection).

\noindent\textbf{Topological Vulnerability:} 1 downstream dependencies.\\ 

Three points `x, y, z` are Bregman-orthogonal if the primal segment from `x` to `y`
is orthogonal to the dual segment from `θ_y` to `θ_z`.
Formally: ⟨∇K(z) - ∇K(y), x - y⟩ = 0.
